claims.text: No product-level confirmation was found on whether the tentsuyu dipping sauce uses standard (wheat-containing) soy sauce or a gluten-free alternative; as a traditional Edomae tempura restaurant it should be assumed to use standard soy sauce unless confirmed otherwise by phone.

name: 豆腐料理 吉座 京王百貨店新宿店 (Tofu Ryori Kichiza (Keio Department Store Sh)

claims.text: No source explicitly states whether wheat-free (tamari-style) soy sauce is available; traditional kaiseki restaurants of this type typically use standard wheat-containing shoyu unless otherwise noted.
Core ingredient (Nikko tofu/yuba) is naturally gluten-free and plant-based, giving a strong base to work from if staff confirm sauce and dashi ingredients.
No dedicated gluten-free fryer or prep line is confirmed; fried toppings are likely cooked in shared equipment.

The restaurant describes its soup as built on dozens of spices plus a "wa-fu dashi" (Japanese-style stock); Japanese-style dashi is conventionally made with bonito flakes (katsuobushi) and/or kelp, and the restaurant does not state that a fish-free or plant-based stock option exists.
The kitchen fries items such as cartilage karaage and cooks all yakitori on a shared charcoal grill; no separate gluten-free preparation area, fryer, or grill section is mentioned anywhere.

The menu's core dishes (oyako-don sauce, yakitori tare, clear soup/broths) are soy- and dashi-based; standard Japanese soy sauce and tare contain wheat, and no wheat-free soy sauce or tare alternative is advertised.
The entire menu is chicken-based (yakitori, oyako-don, mizutaki hot pot); shared grills, fryers, and chicken-bone broths are used throughout with no vegetarian or vegan prep line identified.
No information found on whether vegan drinks/sweets are prepared separately from dairy/egg-containing items in this small shared kitchen.
Cafe lattes can be made with oat milk, soy milk, or almond milk instead of dairy.

name: ヴィーガンカフェ モンキーマジック (Vegan Cafe Monkey Magic (Veganic Monkey Magi)

claims.text: This is a vegan kitchen rather than a certified gluten-free one; no dedicated GF fryer or formal cross-contamination controls were confirmed, so celiac diners should discuss the severity of their needs when booking.

The meat-less nikujaga dish includes kuruma fu (wheat gluten rings), which would not be suitable for those with celiac disease; VegeMap advises choosing a menu only after telling staff about allergies.
Menu features a wheat-gluten rice bowl (車麩丼) and whole-grain wheat gluten (全粒粉車麩); seasonings are naturally-fermented (traditional wheat-containing shoyu).
It is a one-woman operation — Chef Monkey-san does all food preparation and cooking herself — with no mention of gluten-free protocols or cross-contamination controls.
Owner Atsuko Saeki (佐伯敦子) has left veganism personally (脱ヴィーガン) but keeps the menu fully plant-based as a business/food-safety decision, explicitly declining to add fish or meat.
Some dishes may use regular (wheat-containing) soy sauce or other wheat-based ingredients unless you flag this when booking — ask for a wheat-free adjustment in advance.
The restaurant is reservation-only, and the chef designs the tasting course after you tell her about any vegan/vegetarian needs or allergies at the time of booking.
The kitchen is fully vegan — no meat, fish, dairy, or eggs anywhere on the menu — built on naturally cultivated (pesticide- and fertilizer-free) vegetables and additive-free seasonings.

name: ヴェジェトゥス プラス（vegetus+） (Vegetus Plus)

claims.text: Search results across HotPepper, san-tatsu, and generalist directories describe the shop only as offering 'vegan, gluten-free, and takeout' as tag-style options with no detail; explicit statement that results 'do not contain specific information about Celiac disease accommodations, detailed gluten-free menu items, or wheat allergy warnings' and to 'contact the restaurant directly.'

Shop philosophy and preparation detail describe cold-pressed oils, sea salt, unrefined cane sugar, 'no chemical seasonings or preservatives,' and 'all dressings and sauces are homemade' — a natural-food posture with no mention of wheat-free soy sauce, dedicated fryer, or allergen separation.

HappyCow / FindMeGlutenFree celiac-review search for 'Vegetus Plus Suidobashi gluten free celiac' returned no listing or celiac review for this specific shop — only unrelated dedicated-GF venues (Gluten Free T's Kitchen, Gluten Free 61).

Shop's self-described concept is 'vegetables plus' animal protein/fat with a daily-changing deli of ~10 items mixing vegan and non-vegan dishes; no confirmation that vegan items avoid dashi/bonito or that non-vegan dashi is kept separate.

Meals are made with organic and low-pesticide vegetables, brown rice, and homemade dressings/sauces with no preservatives or chemical seasoning, and the shop explicitly lists vegan and gluten-free options among its rotating deli dishes.

name: 焼き鳥 鳥たん 水道橋店 (Yakitori Toritan Suidobashi)

claims.text: Yakitori tare glazes are conventionally wheat-based soy sauce; no gluten-free tare or shoyu alternative was mentioned in any source found for this restaurant.
